The five ordered vertices of T+εQ give shoelace area 1+3ε+ε². The proposed enclosing triangle exceeds this by 5ε²/4. At each middle candidate a through-point barycentric apex cap in the triangle has area at most 4/9 of its area. Scaling the excess by 1/4 gives the bound 5ε²/36 and total bound 7ε²/36.

A fixed inscribed disk and an enclosing competitor bound each vertex of every area-bounded enclosing triangle by the exterior vertex-to-diameter area. This yields attainment and compactness. Equality of the support sum with its square value would force both axes as edges and the intercepts 3/2,3. Their triangle has area 9/4>2, proving an attained positive gap on the whole competitor class.

The merged normal list gives quadratic Minkowski area. Swept strips over the edges supply the first-order coefficient with overlap only within O(ε) of the vertices, and the parallel support triangle gives the matching upper coefficient. For the displayed T the coefficient is exactly p_T.

Minimum endpoint containers are T and εS with S in the compact gap class. Their Minkowski midpoint lies in the actual new middle fiber whatever its own selected container. Subtraction gives cost at least αε/4, so the ratio is at least 9α/(7ε). Binary padded layers cannot mix, making the bound uniform over independent choices.
The cited source sections distinguish this endpoint-generated construction from the previously accepted arbitrary-container counterexample.
